R781.note: htmlspecialchars(ENT_QUOTES,'UTF-8') on the exact echoed value; no other change.

R782.note: can:refund,order middleware + Policy checking order ownership; controller/response untouched, matches contract.

R783.note: Full-match RFC5322-style regex rejects CRLF/anything non-email before the address ever reaches the socket; legitimate emails unaffected.

R785.note: Moves storage outside the static root, derives extension from detected MIME, serves via an authenticated download route with attachment/nosniff/CSP headers; matches the JSON-url/400-shape contract.

R786.note: Adds Secure/HttpOnly/SameSite; cookie Name/Value/Path contract unchanged.

R787.note: Removes the whole .csrf(ignoringRequestMatchers(...)) customizer so Spring's default (enabled) CSRF applies; no other route affected.

R788.note: Table name resolved through a server-side allowlist map; bound accountId/status untouched. Two extra table names beyond ledger_entries are invented rather than sourced from the case, but this is disclosed and harmless.

R789.note: Narrows the exclusion to /api/webhooks/** exactly as the code's own comment intends.

R790.note: subprocess.run with an argument array and shell=False closes the reported shell-injection vector, but the write-up's explanation falsely claims the regex '[a-zA-Z0-9._:-]+' rejects hostnames starting with '-' — it does not (leading '-' is an allowed character), so the argument-injection gap it claims to close is still open.

R791.note: Two options given; the interim validation (reject CRLF, allowlist chars) fully closes the vector while preserving the Socket signature. Primary Jakarta Mail option changes the method signature entirely but is clearly labeled as an alternative.

R792.note: escapeshellarg() on the host argument; output/return behavior unchanged.

R794.note: allowed_classes=>false blocks object-injection/gadget RCE, but the stated contract requires unsigned cookies to never reach unserialize() at all; no HMAC/signature check is added, so a forged array-only cookie (e.g. fabricated coupon/items) is still deserialized and accepted.

R795.note: ldap.escapeFilterAttribute() on the filter value; response shape unchanged.

R796.note: Adds the missing $_FILES['avatar']['error'] !== UPLOAD_ERR_OK check before the mime/move steps, exactly matching the reported gap.

R797.note: Builds the filter as an ldapjs EqualityFilter object instead of a string, structurally avoiding filter-syntax injection; passed directly to client.search().

R798.note: store.New() is a no-op here: gorilla/sessions' CookieStore.Get() calls store.New() internally when the session isn't already cached in the request registry, so New() decodes the same pre-existing/planted cookie exactly like Get() does. The session fixation is not fixed. No new side effects are introduced (behavior is otherwise unchanged), so legitimate login still works.

R799.note: Captures erase()'s return value and only advances manually on the no-erase branch; visits every element once, preserves order.

R800.note: Allowlist maps the request plugin name to a fixed module path; unknown names rejected with 400 instead of importing arbitrary modules.

R801.note: Replaces hand-built RESP/inline text with StackExchange.Redis's StringSet (length-prefixed, no CRLF injection possible). DI constructor type change (Socket -> IConnectionMultiplexer) is explicitly called out as a required change.

R802.note: HTML::Entities::encode_entities() on the interpolated value; output structure otherwise unchanged.

R803.note: toRealPath() requires the target to already exist, but the extraction target file does not exist until Files.copy() writes it — canonicalizing it beforehand throws NoSuchFileException for every ordinary, non-malicious entry, breaking normal extraction entirely. This isn't disclosed; the write-up presents the code as fully preserving valid extraction, which it does not.

R804.note: execFile() with an argument array plus a strict character allowlist for reportName; response behavior otherwise unchanged. Allowlist narrows previously-accepted report-name characters, but this is shown plainly in the diff.

R805.note: Rejects both an explicit scheme and a non-null host, correctly also blocking protocol-relative '//evil.com' redirects, not just scheme-prefixed ones.

R806.note: Rejects separators/'.'/'..' in the filename and independently verifies realpath containment; Content-Disposition also switched to the canonical basename.

R807.note: resize(count) fixes the packet[i] write, but count is never validated against fields.size(), so fields[i] remains an out-of-bounds read for count>fields.size() — exactly the case the file's own contract required to be rejected or reported rather than silently allowed.

R808.note: SecureRandom with 16 random bytes, URL-safe Base64; cookie/session wiring otherwise untouched.

R809.note: Standard RFC4515 hex-escaping of LDAP filter metacharacters before concatenation.

R810.note: Rejects CR/LF/NUL in the filename before building the RETR command line.

R811.note: Saves the offset before realloc and recomputes the pointer afterward — the canonical safe pattern for this exact bug.

R812.note: secrets.choice() replacing random.choice(); same 32-char alphabet, same response/dict shape.

R813.note: mathjs evaluate() (pinned to a recent, post-sandbox-fix major version) replaces eval(); invalid expressions now return a controlled 400 instead of an uncaught exception, disclosed in the diff.

R814.note: Applies the file's own existing escapeAuthorName() to rawComment, consistent with how authorName is already handled; minimal, correctly scoped diff.

R815.note: SimpleEvaluationContext.forReadOnlyDataBinding() blocks constructors/type-refs/bean-refs and (absent an explicit method resolver) method invocation, but the case explicitly names 'using SimpleEvaluationContext as a claimed sandbox for arbitrary untrusted expressions' as the trap; the intended fix is a deny-by-default, narrowly-scoped expression grammar rather than relying on SpEL's own restricted-context feature. Legitimate arithmetic previews still work.

R816.note: Allowlist maps exactly to the two functions that actually exist in the file (clearCache, purgeSessions); unknown commands now get a clean message instead of a fatal undefined-function error.

R817.note: Rejects space/CR/LF in the cache key while still permitting the ':'-containing key format the file's own comment describes.

R818.note: session_regenerate_id(true) called right after password_verify succeeds, before any $_SESSION writes — correctly rotates the PHP session id and destroys the old session data.

R819.note: ProcessBuilder with a separate-argument array plus an explicit host.startsWith("-") rejection actually implements the leading-dash defense it describes (unlike R790's equivalent claim).

R820.note: The scheme check only runs when the input contains '://', but classic javascript:/data: XSS payloads (e.g. 'javascript:alert(1)') don't contain '://', so they skip validation entirely and reach the href unmodified — the reported vector is not closed. Legitimate http/https links (which do contain '://') and unaffected mailto links keep working.
